content:
If you've just bought a new Mac, such as the recently released Mac mini or Mac Studio, you're likely on the hunt for a new external display.

Here are my recommendations, covering a wide range of product categories, price points, and more.

The best external Mac monitors

Apple Studio Display

When it comes to the best monitors on the market, the Apple Studio Display simply can't be left out. While it's on the pricier side, it features Apple's signature gorgeous design and comes with a 27-inch 5K display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Color support: Wide color gamut (P3), supports 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with Desk View
  • True Tone technology: Automatically adjusts the display's color temperature based on ambient lighting
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host charging: Up to 96W

The Studio Display comes in several configurations at different price points, which I'll list below. If you're after an iMac-like experience to match your Mac, nothing comes close to the Apple Studio Display.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

The Studio Display XDR launched earlier this year and offers several major upgrades over the standard Studio Display, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: Up to 1,000 nits SDR, up to 2,000 nits HDR peak
  • Color support: Wide P3 and Adobe RGB color gamuts, supports 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 120Hz with Adaptive Sync
  • Host charging: Up to 140W

Of course, these advantages come at a higher price than the standard Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor is a pretty compelling option for Mac users, thanks to its 4K OLED panel. My 9to5Toys colleague Justin Kahn has already made the switch to this monitor, and he says, "using it with my Mac mini over the past few months has been an absolute treat."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution) with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2 USB-A
  • Built-in camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

Although its resolution isn't as sharp as some of the 5K or 6K options on this list, you'll get to enjoy all the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks, better color reproduction, and improved contrast.

Buy the Samsung M9 OLED Smart Monitor:

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K represents LG's evolution in the high-end monitor market. It features a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels, plus a full array of ports. Here are the key specs:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 450 nits typical; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, supports 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • True Tone: None; supports automatic brightness adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports, and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast ratio: 2,000:1

Find purchase links for the LG UltraFine 6K below

Asus ProArt 5K Display

My colleague Jeff Benjamin got hands-on with this monitor, and it immediately caught my eye. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) Display 5K delivers the same 5K resolution as the Studio Display (5120×2880) in a 27-inch form factor, but at half the price.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB, and 95% Adobe RGB, supports 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustments: Ambient light and backlight sensors automatically adjust brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: One USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

Check out Jeff's full review for all the details. If you want a 5K display to pair with your Mac, the Asus ProArt is an unbeatable option.

Find purchase links for the Asus ProArt Display 5K below:

Asus ProArt 6K Display

If you want a larger size with higher resolution, Asus has you covered too. The new Asus ProArt Display 6K (PA32QCV) is a 32-inch display with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "absurdly good value" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical, 600 nits HDR peak; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, supports 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync (48–60Hz)
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub connections, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

Perhaps the most appealing aspect of the ASUS ProArt 6K Display is its price. Compared to some of the most popular 4K and 5K displays on the market, it's priced significantly lower.

Find purchase links for the ASUS ProArt 6K display below:

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

Samsung's ViewFinity S8 5K is another attractive option for pairing with your new Mac, offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: 350 nits typical
  • Color support: 99% sRGB, supports 1.07 billion colors; HDR10
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustments: Adaptive Picture automatically adjusts brightness based on ambient lighting
  • Ports: One USB-C port with 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A ports, one downstream USB-C port, Ethernet, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Find purchase links for the Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K below:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt Monitor

This might just be my current favorite option. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor comes packed with Mac-friendly features, and of course the standout highlight is the crisp 5K resolution.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical and peak; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Color support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709, and 98% P3, supports 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one downstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one upstream USB-C port, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: Physical external controller with customizable controls

Find purchase links for the BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor below:

For more, check out our full review: BenQ's 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 designer monitor is a true Apple Studio Display competitor

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Monitor

If you're looking for a 32-inch monitor for your new Mac but want to stay under $1,000, this is one of the most appealing options. The biggest downside is that you're "only" getting 4K resolution rather than 5K. But it more than makes up for it with a wide selection of ports, and a 32-inch panel under $1,000 is hard to beat.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch
  • Color support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supports 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustments: No automatic ambient light color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3 ports, two HDMI 2.0 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, USB-B, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

Find purchase links for the BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt monitor below:

For more, check out our full review: Should 32-inch 4K Mac monitors really be ruled out?

Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultrawide Monitor

If you want to pair an ultrawide monitor with your Mac, the Dell U4025QW is easily one of the best options on the market. It packs 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate into a 40-inch display. It also comes with a full array of ports, an anti-glare screen, and more.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2,500R curvature
  • Brightness: 450 nits typical, 600 nits HDR peak; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supports 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: Up to 120Hz with VRR support
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustments: Ambient light sensor automatically adjusts brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C ports, five USB-A ports, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and audio output
  • Host charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Find purchase links for the Dell U4025QW 40-inch ultrawide monitor below:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

If you want to get into the ultrawide monitor market at a more affordable price, the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC is an option, and it's currently on sale at nearly half price. It's not as feature-packed as some of the other options, but you still get a 34-inch ultrawide curved display and a variety of ports, including a Thunderbolt 4 port with power delivery.

  • Display: 34-inch ultrawide curved display, Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440), 1,000R curvature for an immersive viewing experience.
  • Brightness: 350 nits typical.
  • Camera: None.
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (supports up to 90W power delivery), one HDMI 2.0 port, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0 ports, one RJ45 Ethernet port, and one 3.5mm headphone jack.

Find purchase links for the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC below:

Wrapping up

These are just some of the standout external monitor options to pair with your new Mac. They all offer excellent macOS integration, plenty of connectivity options, and unique sizes and form factors.

Have you recently bought a new Mac? Which monitor are you pairing it with? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
